morning.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
morning.body: Mortgage rates: 7.32% published 2026-10-22, modeled 7.32% today. 10-year Treasury: 4.96% (-17 bp). MBS: 15.50 ticks. Rate bias: Improving. The mortgage spread is 236 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: Core PCE Price Index on 10-28. Biggest risk: Core PCE Price Index. A hot print reverses any Treasury rally. What LOs should know: pull your float list and re-price. Improvements reach rate sheets with a one to two day lag

eod.title: END OF DAY REVIEW
eod.what_moved: Mortgage rates are improving. The 10-year Treasury is 4.96% (-17 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.32%.
eod.why: The 10-year Treasury is at 4.96%, -17 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved -8 bp. That breaks down exactly: -14 bp from Treasuries and +6 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 236 bp, which is normal and sits at the 69th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 28 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.
eod.reprice_caveat: Real reprice detection needs a live MBS feed. This is inferred from the modeled tick move.
eod.expectations_change: The 2-year moved -16 bp, which means the market softened its expected path for Fed policy.
